newsitem.title: IRAN: Key events since Iran's revolution.
newsitem.headline: Key events since Iran's revolution.

text.p: Following are highlights of key events in Iran since the overthrow of the Shah in 1979 by Islamic fundamentalists:

1979 - Revolution led by Shi'ite Moslem clergymen topples U.S.-backed Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi. Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini emerges as spiritual leader and returns from 15 years' exile. Islamic republic proclaimed after referendum. Militant students demand Washington return exiled Shah for trial and seize U.S. embassy in Tehran. Some 52 Americans are captured and will be held hostage for 444 days.
1980 - Secret U.S. military mission to rescue hostages ends in disaster in sandstorm in central Iranian desert. Shah dies of cancer in Egypt. Iran-Iraq war starts after border skirmishes.

1981 - Khomeini's fundamentalist followers gradually push liberals out of government and oust revolutionary Iran's first elected president Abolhassan Bani-Sadr. He flees to France. Senior officials including a president, a prime minister and a chief justice are killed in a series of bomb attacks before armed opposition, mainly from radical Islamist Mujaideen Khalq and autonomy-seeking Kurdish groups, is crushed.

1986 - Secret U.S. contacts with Iran are revealed. U.S. secretly sold arms in exchange for Tehran's help in freeing American hostages held by pro-Iranian militants in Lebanon. The deal, and subsequent revelations that profits were illegally channelled to Nicaraguan rebels create the biggest crisis of Ronald Reagan's U.S. presidency.
1987 - U.S. forces engage in series of encounters with Iranian forces, including strikes on Gulf oil platforms being used as bases.

1988 - In biggest clash, six Iranian vessels are sunk or damaged and a U.S. helicopter is downed after U.S. warships demolish two Iranian oil rigs in retaliation for mine blast which holed U.S. frigate. U.S. cruiser Vincennes shoots down Iran Air Airbus over the Gulf, killing all 290 people on board. Washington says it was a mistake. Iran calls it murder. U.N.-brokered ceasefire halts Iran-Iraq war after death of an estimated million people over eight years.

1989 - Khomeini orders Moslems to kill British author Salman Rushdie for blaspheming Islam in his book "The Satanic Verses". Khomeini dies 11 days after surgery to remove cancerous third of his stomach. President Ali Khamenei is chosen as Khomeini's spiritual successor and supreme leader. Parliamentary speaker Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani is elected president by a landslide.
1990 - Iran stays neutral when Iraq invades Kuwait, denouncing both Baghdad's conquest of Kuwait and any long-term presence of U.S. forces in the region.
1993 - U.S. President Bill Clinton takes office, launches drive to isolate Iran for supporting "terrorism", seeking nuclear arms and trying to wreck Middlem East peace efforts.

1995 - Clinton imposes oil and trade sanctions against Iran for alleged sponsorship of "terrorism", seeking to acquire nuclear arms, and hostility to the Middle East peace process. Iran denies the charges.
1996 - Clinton stiffens sanctions with penalties against any firm that invests $40 million or more a year in oil and gas projects in Iran and Libya.

1997 - German court concludes top Iranian leadership ordered 1992 assassination of Kurdish dissidents in Berlin. European Union withdraws ambassadors from Tehran. Mohammad Khatami elected president by landslide which buries favourite, conservative parliamentary speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri.
